caveats: Requires two concurrent image-create requests for the same product (for example two staff POSTs to product_image_edit with img_pk None), each in its own DB transaction/connection.
Depends on the database running under read-committed isolation (or autocommit), so a SELECT MAX does not see the other transaction's uncommitted INSERT.
Depends on blocking DB I/O releasing the GIL for same-process threads to interleave; separate workers or processes interleave regardless of the GIL.
subclaims.reason: Two concurrent POSTs to dashboard product_image_edit for the same product with img_pk None each build ProductImage(product=product) (saleor/dashboard/product/views.py:139) with order unset and reach ProductImage.save through ProductImageForm.save (saleor/dashboard/product/views.py:143; saleor/dashboard/product/forms.py:165). Each new save with order None (saleor/product/models/images.py:39) runs SELECT MAX(order) over that product's images (saleor/product/models/images.py:40-41) and then INSERTs with order max plus one (saleor/product/models/images.py:43-44). Nothing serializes the read plus write: there is no select_for_update, no transaction.atomic around save, and Meta declares only ordering with no uniqueness on product and order (saleor/product/models/images.py:31-33). If both SELECT MAX statements run before either INSERT commits, under read-committed neither sees the other's uncommitted row, so both compute the same max plus one and insert duplicate order values. The switch point is blocking DB I/O between the SELECT and the INSERT, which releases the GIL, so CPython threads can interleave there and separate workers or processes trivially can.
